rules.title: Home Office fees from 8 April 2026
rules.text: Sponsor licence: £611 for small businesses and charities, or £1,682 for medium and large businesses. Certificate of Sponsorship: £525 each. Immigration Skills Charge: £480 a year for small sponsors or £1,320 for medium and large, paid upfront for the visa length.

rules.title: Compliance visits
rules.text: The Home Office can visit before or after granting a licence, sometimes unannounced. [Read about compliance](/sponsor-licence-compliance/)

rules.title: Right to work checks
rules.text: Sponsors must check every employee’s right to work, not just sponsored workers. [Read our guide](/right-to-work-checks/)

boxTitle: Want a second pair of eyes before you apply?
boxText: A consultation costs far less than a refused application. We’ll check your case against the current rules and tell you honestly where you stand.

sections.heading: Who needs a sponsor licence?
sections.text: Any UK employer that wants to hire someone from overseas on a Skilled Worker visa, or on most other work routes, needs a sponsor licence first. That includes workers already in the UK on another visa, such as a Student or Graduate visa, who want to switch. You don’t need a licence to employ British or Irish citizens, people with ILR or settled status, or people whose visa already lets them work for any employer.

faqs.q: How much does a sponsor licence cost?
faqs.a: £611 for small businesses and charities, or £1,682 for medium and large businesses, plus £525 per Certificate of Sponsorship and the Immigration Skills Charge.

faqs.q: How long does a sponsor licence take?
faqs.a: The Home Office aims to decide most applications within 8 weeks, or faster with the optional £750 priority service.

faqs.q: How long does a sponsor licence last?
faqs.a: It no longer needs renewing every 4 years under the current rules, but you must keep meeting your duties.
